content: 1. When coughing or sneezing, always do so into your arm or use a tissue, which should be discarded immediately after use. 2. Standard precautions must be maintained at all times and for all patients to prevent infection. 3. Handle needles, scalpels, and other sharp instruments with care during use, cleaning, and disposal to prevent injuries. 4. Do not bend, break, or manipulate used needles or sharp instruments. Avoid recapping needles. 5. Always have a sharps container nearby when administering injections, and immediately discard single-use needles and syringes into the container without recapping or passing them to another person. 6. Sharps containers should be sealed and sent for incineration when they are three-quarters full. 7. Wear full personal protective equipment (PPE), including heavy-duty or rubber gloves, when cleaning the environment or handling infectious waste. 8. Ensure proper waste management by segregating waste at the point of generation to enable safe handling. 9. Place sharp objects like needles, syringes, and glass articles in puncture-resistant containers. 10. Collect solid, non-sharp infectious waste in leak-proof bags placed in covered bins. 11. Discard single-use items properly to prevent cross-contamination. 12. Clean and disinfect environmental surfaces and frequently touched areas using appropriate procedures. 13. Clean floors and horizontal surfaces at least once daily or whenever soiled, always working from clean to dirty areas to prevent contamination transfer. 14. Avoid dry sweeping or shaking out dusty rags, as this can aerosolize contaminants. Use moistened cloths for cleaning to minimize airborne particles. 15. Always clean surfaces before applying disinfectants to prevent inactivation of disinfectants by organic matter. 16. Change cleaning solutions and equipment frequently to avoid contamination. 17. WHO discourages spraying disinfectants in clinical areas, as it is potentially dangerous and has no proven disease control benefit. 18. Handle contaminated linens with full PPE, including heavy-duty gloves and aprons, to prevent skin and mucous membrane exposure. 19. Place used linens in durable bags or containers for transport. Heavily soiled linens should be incinerated if manipulation is not feasible. 20. If washing linens by hand, soak them in water and soap, then disinfect with a 0.05% chlorine solution for 15 minutes before rinsing and drying. Avoid splashing during the process. 21. Clean and disinfect patient care equipment contaminated with blood, body fluids, or secretions to reduce exposure risks. 22. Reusable equipment must be cleaned, disinfected, sterilized, and reprocessed before use with another patient. 23. Disposable items with sharp edges, such as needles and syringes, must be immediately disposed of in puncture-resistant, leak-proof sharps containers. Final disposal should include incineration. 24. During viral hemorrhagic fever (VHF) outbreaks, PPE is essential to protect healthcare workers and patients from contamination. 25. PPE must be donned and doffed carefully under the supervision of a trained observer to avoid self-contamination. 26. Always protect the eyes, nose, and mouth when using PPE, and never touch your face with gloved hands. 27. Ensure adequate supplies, proper staff training, and close supervision for the safe and effective use of PPE. 28. When donning PPE, remove all personal items, wear a scrub suit and rubber boots, and ensure all PPE fits correctly. 29. Perform hand hygiene before putting on gloves, coveralls, masks, face shields, and aprons. 30. Conduct a self-check in a mirror and have a buddy verify the PPE is properly donned. 31. When removing PPE, do so under supervision, ensuring infectious waste containers are available for safe disposal. 32. Remove aprons, head and neck coverings, coveralls, and gloves carefully to avoid contamination. 33. Perform hand hygiene between each step of PPE removal. 34. Avoid spraying disinfectants during PPE removal unless necessary, and only spray below the nipple line to minimize splashing. 35. Dispose of all PPE safely and ensure reusable items are cleaned and disinfected appropriately.
